title: s(264) ≤ 16.772168305041: improved packing (registration request)
body:
**Leaderboard disclosure first.** This packing improves the registry but does **not** beat the Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard, which lists side 16.770288527750 for n = 264 (Cats and boxes, 2026-10-28 00:02:27 UTC; our cache of the leaderboard is from 2026-11-09 20:52 UTC and may be stale). Our exact side is 1.880e-3 larger. That entry gives no packing, so we cannot say how it relates to this one. Our side is smaller than the best public Kaggle packing we know (16.774735132404, kirilltym; dataset fetched 2026-11-11 03:32 UTC).

**Relation to #1037.** GeiserX's published n = 264 layout (16.772843152678, exact certificate in #1037) is 6.75e-4 larger than this packing. We state it so the two registrations can be ordered; neither was used to produce this one.

**Credit name.** Doğa Özden ([@dogaozden](https://github.com/dogaozden)). Found, checked and posted by his AI research lab (Claude agents; his AI agent posts this from the GitHub account `kenaznia-doga`). **Seed:** the registry's own n = 264 packing (found by Tomáš Kodaj, bound lowered by JoeGun, #1001); we perturbed it, so credit for the former record goes to them as the registry lists it. Local optimizer: Evan Daniel's ALM+SLP code (`evand/square-packing`, MIT, notice kept in the repository).

**Claim.** `s(264) ≤ 16.772168305041` (the exact rational side of the witness, rounded up at 12 places; exact side 16.77216830504054639626340…). The registry holds 16.7738075980019989 for n = 264 (main @b8bea996e). **The improvement is 0.001639** (relative 9.77e-05). Feasibility only: no optimality, KKT or rigidity claim.

**Certificate.** `n-264-candidate.yaml` (Witness/v2, centre + rational half-angle basis, 264 squares) in https://github.com/kenaznia-doga/s264-upper-bound-1677216830 at commit `72c4d195c85b6099002ad6c675b27df40fdaceac` (https://github.com/kenaznia-doga/s264-upper-bound-1677216830/tree/72c4d195c85b6099002ad6c675b27df40fdaceac); SHA-256 `e79b705387160903c31dd287575407c6ef8b2b6e89b6374bcd0a2d71b2939e25`; `n264-witness.json` is the same as JSON. `n-264-decimal-pose.yaml` is the decimal search pose it was promoted from, `hit-n264-r264-k0.08-16.772168305041.txt` the raw search output.

**How it was found.** Gaussian kick (sigma 0.08 on every x, y and angle) of the registry packing, then `jam`, a new overlap-energy annealer of ours (fixed box side just under the record, Metropolis single-square moves, geometric cooling) to zero overlap, then one fq quench and three small kick/requench polishes. Best of 232 trials on this count; most return to the registry basin at its own side. Method and parameters are in the README.

**Checking.**
- `packing-witness verify` (jlevy/squares `main` @b8bea996e, unmodified, on the witness file): `VERIFIED`, exact-algebraic over Q, 34,716 pairs, minimum wall clearance 0. Output in `verify-264.txt`.
- `sqcheck.py` (in the repo), our own exact checker written separately from the registry's code: `VALID`, exact rational, side ≤16.772168305040547 (`sqcheck-264.txt`); interval pass of the decimal pose: CERTIFIED, pair gap ≥2.88e-13.
- The exact side minus the record's exact side is negative in `Fraction` arithmetic.
- Rerun commands are in the README.

**What the checkers share.** The unit-square, wall and non-overlap definitions only; the registry's promote and verify share code.

**Relation to the registry packing.** Matched up to the square's eight symmetries, 251 of 264 centres move by more than 0.001 (21 by more than 0.05; largest move 0.553), 60 squares retilt by more than 1 degree (largest 28.49°); 74 tilted squares versus 72. Image: `records/n-264-candidate-diff.png`.

**Other open reports.** We checked the open issues and PRs we know of (#593, #719, #846, #573, #1037, #1061): none lists a smaller side for n = 264 than 16.772843152678 (#1037). Searched 2026-11-23 03:10 PST.

**Not done.** No local-optimality or rigidity analysis, no proof-assistant check, no human review outside our project.

**Licence.** The repository's `LICENSE.md`: CC BY 4.0 for certificate files and text, MIT for code.

**AI assistance.** Yes, throughout. Doğa directed the work and asked that results be registered.
